title: Fidelity-Based Robustness Margins for Finite-Time Quantum Control
authors: S. P. O'Neil, F. C. Langbein, C. A. Weidner, E. A. Jonckheere, S. Schirmer
abstract: We develop a structure-specific fidelity-threshold robustness margin for finite-dimensional closed quantum systems under piecewise-constant coherent control. A scalar physical parameter may perturb the drift, a control Hamiltonian, or another declared Hamiltonian component across the control horizon. A differential sensitivity bound for trace-amplitude gate fidelity yields a threshold-dependent Lipschitz constant on the connected safe parameter component and hence a certified finite perturbation radius. Recentering this certificate produces an iterative one-dimensional method that takes certified safe steps toward the first fidelity-threshold boundary in either parameter direction. A three-qubit gate-control example shows that these finite margins vary by up to a factor of three across controllers of comparable nominal fidelity and contain structure-dependent information not captured by nominal differential sensitivity alone.
summary: This paper introduces a novel framework to calculate robust margins for quantum gate fidelity when system parameters are uncertain. By deriving structure-specific Lipschitz bounds, it certifies the maximum allowed perturbation size while guaranteeing the final gate fidelity stays above a set threshold. This moves beyond simple local sensitivity analysis by providing actionable safety boundaries for quantum control protocols.
main_problem: The paper develops a method to quantify the robustness margin for finite-time quantum control when the system Hamiltonian is subject to structured, small perturbations.
main_result: A structure-specific fidelity-threshold robustness margin is derived, providing a certified minimum perturbation radius ensuring gate fidelity remains above a specified threshold $F_T$.
method: The analysis uses differential sensitivity bounds and establishes a Lipschitz constant for the fidelity function with respect to the perturbing parameter. An iterative algorithm refines this margin by taking safe steps toward the first boundary.
model_or_system: The system is a finite-dimensional closed quantum system evolving under piecewise-constant coherent control, governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian that includes structured affine perturbations from a single scalar parameter $\mu$.
key_observables: Normalized trace-amplitude gate fidelity ($F(t_f)$), the sensitivity of fidelity to perturbation ($\zeta_\mu^0$), and the certified robust margin ($M$).
important_parameters: The control time horizon $t_f$, the target fidelity threshold $F_T$, and the magnitude of the structured Hamiltonian perturbations $\mu$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to scalar, one-parameter structured Hamiltonian perturbations; it does not cover simultaneous multi-parameter uncertainty or open-system dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate fidelity error trajectories under various perturbations ($H_0, H_1, H_2$) and compare the calculated robustness margins ($M$) against the nominal differential sensitivity magnitudes ($|\zeta_j|$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using fidelity derivatives to derive a finite margin certificate. It then applies this method to specific three-qubit gate control examples, comparing the resulting structure-dependent margins across different perturbation types.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, quantifiable guarantees on the stability of quantum gates under realistic parameter uncertainties, which is crucial for designing fault-tolerant quantum hardware and understanding experimental limitations in quantum computation.
